$doc: The assistant surface's appearance, as data — the source of the `@component chat` block in css/components.css and of dist/react/chat.tsx. IT IS THE BLOCK WITH THE MOST RULES IN THE FILE, and the striking thing about transcribing it is how little it needed: four members of one enum, two names in another, and a shape for a pseudo-element that belongs to a rule rather than to a tag path. Everything else was already sayable — the states, the scoped parts, the `:empty` thread, the keyframes, the query-only send button. `chat` is where the method PATTERNS.md argues for stops producing findings and starts producing transcriptions, which is the result a migration wants from its largest block.

block.title: Chat
note: The assistant surface: turn list, composer, streaming state and a
collapsible tool trace. Lives inside a `.band`/`.well` like any other
section — it is a section of the page, not a widget floating over it.
The thread has a max-height and scrolls internally. That is not
cosmetic: a rail cannot size the band (its only child is out of
flow — components/skeleton/spec.md), and a bounded thread stops the
WELL doing it instead. A conversation of any length leaves the band
exactly as tall as it started.
Every colour here is a semantic token. There is no
`prefers-color-scheme` query in this file and adding one would be a
bug — a colour that differs in dark is a `dark` value in tokens.json.

rules.name: turn-user
rules.$doc: A PART AND NOT A VARIANT, and the reason is structural rather than a judgement about what a user turn is: a modifier's selector is its ROOT plus its name, and this component's root is `.chat`. `.chat__turn--user` modifies a part, and a part has no axis — a companion selector that needs one is a component with its own definition, which is the line that has held through sixteen blocks. So the two turn kinds are two parts, exactly as the stylesheet writes them.

rules.name: turn-assistant
rules.$doc: The assistant turn declares nothing of its own — a SCOPE, exactly as `.drawer .profile > div` is. Its whole effect is the role label inside it turning accent, which is the rule below.

rules.name: prose
note: The only model-authored text on the page.

rules.name: why
note: One clause on why a project answers the question — model-authored,
so it reads as annotation rather than as the project's own copy.

rules.name: note
note: A neutral notice: "Stopped.", or a deadline reached with partial content
already on screen. Deliberately NOT the error's framed box. An error is
framed because something went wrong and the frame is the alarm; a note is
the surface reporting what it did, and a reader who pressed Stop must not
be shown their own decision dressed as a failure. So: label colour, no
frame, no border — chrome, at the weight of chrome.

rules.name: state
note: ---- Streaming state ----
Four squares from the same vocabulary as the skeleton's automata, so
"thinking" reads as this site rather than as a generic spinner.

rules.name: trace
note: ---- Tool trace ----
Open while the answer streams, collapsed the moment it completes. The
trace is evidence, not narration — but evidence arriving live is the
only thing on screen during the wait, so it earns the space until there
is an answer to give it back to. Collapsing on completion is also what
keeps it out of the log's single completion announcement.

rules.name: trace-marker
rules.$doc: The vendor pseudo, as-spelled. `list-style: none` above is what removes the standard marker; WebKit draws its disclosure triangle through this one instead, and the standard `::marker` does not reach it. A closed enum takes the name verbatim rather than teaching the format about vendor prefixes.

rules.name: trace-open
rules.$doc: A SCOPE and not an appearance — the open trace declares nothing itself; its whole effect is the arrow below it turning down. A state with no declarations is not a shape this format has, so it carries the one declaration the stylesheet gives it… which it does not. See `trace-open-arrow`: the rule the file writes is `.chat__trace[open] .chat__trace-toggle::before`, and the state exists so that selector can be named.

rules.name: form
note: ---- Composer ----

rules.name: input-busy
note: Busy, not disabled. js/chat.js sets `aria-disabled` + `readOnly` and never
the `disabled` attribute: disabling the focused textarea drops focus to
<body> and re-enabling it does not put focus back, which strands the reader
at the top of a very long document. Because the field now KEEPS focus while
it is inert, the state needs a visible colour more than it did before.

rules.name: suggest
note: Prompts that seed the first question. Chips are display-only by
contract, so a suggestion the visitor can press is a small Button.

rules.name: send
rules.$doc: QUERY-ONLY. The submit button is a `.btn.btn--solid` at every width and the composer's own class says one thing about it and only on a phone: span the row it now has to itself. There is no unconditional `.chat__send` rule for an override to name, which is the construct `nav` forced.
